Legacy quick cards

Quick References

Quick reference

Player-Safe Premise

Player-safePrint-readyTV-safe

You are contractors or trusted associates delivering a sealed package through Sablewood to Hush. Marlowe Fairwind is a playable pregen and the default package custodian; Sabine Quillon is only an optional backup NPC contact for the S00-01 job scene. The job begins inside the system, not outside it.

Quick reference

Goldspire Delivery Contract

Player-safePrint-ready

Route assurance contract for sealed ward-related cargo. Liability language is optimistic; the missing risks are the point.

Quick reference

Incident Response Placard

Player-safePrint-ready

If found, preserve cargo value, identify reimbursable losses, and await authorized incident classification.

Quick reference

Route Ledger

Player-safePrint-readySpoilers

The ledger times do not match the official route. Someone altered the logistics trail before the cart was found.

Quick reference

Bramble Evidence Slips

GM-onlyPrint-readySpoilers

Signal knots, old road-crew tags, charm-stone armor, and a route sketch reveal grievance without excusing murder.

Quick reference

Hush Welcome Card

Player-safeTV-safe

Welcome to Hush. Shoes off at the Co-op. If your boots are returned cleaner than you left them, say thank you twice.

Quick reference

Clover Co-op Gift Table

Player-safePrint-ready

Warm rolls, moss-honey, clover cord bracelet, safe-path directions, antiseptic moss, and a quiet warning about the Custodian.

Quick reference

Keystone Warning Label

Player-safePrint-readySpoilers

Do not open near unstable ward lines. Do not strike. Do not cast strong magic within arm's reach unless a keeper says the stone is listening.

Quick reference

Open Vale Ritual Reference

GM-onlyPrint-readySpoilers

Protect the Custodian, hold the ward lines, track the countdown, and spend Fear when old obligations answer the ritual.

Quick reference

GM Quick Sheet

GM-onlyPrint-ready

Very Easy 5, Easy 10, Average 15, Hard 20, Very Hard 25, Nearly Impossible 30. On Fear, make risk visible before making it worse. Spend Fear to split attention, threaten cargo, advance countdowns, expose costs, or activate environment pressure.

Quick reference

Condition / Hope / Fear Cheat Sheet

Player-safePrint-readyTV-safe

Hope improves position, reveals a clean truth, or gives a boon. Fear succeeds with cost, invites a move, or advances a visible threat. The official global conditions are Hidden, Restrained, and Vulnerable.

Quick reference

Character / Pregen Selection Handout

Player-safePrint-ready

Choose a pregen as written, reskin flavor, lightly tweak identity/Experience wording, or use full custom only if the table has dedicated build time.

Quick reference

Session Zero Worksheet

Player-safePrint-ready

Write each PC's reason for taking the job, one relationship to another PC, one corporation they distrust or rely on, and one line of intent.

Quick reference

Connection Question Cards

Player-safePrint-ready

Ask another PC: We ran a delivery that went wrong before. What did we agree never to tell anyone? Which one of us still believes the system can be made decent?

Quick reference

Duality Dice / Hope-Fear Cheat Sheet

Player-safePrint-readyTV-safe

Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add a trait, compare to the Difficulty. Higher die sets Hope/Fear. Doubles are Critical Success.

Quick reference

Roll Outcome Options

Player-safePrint-ready

Use the listed DC, then choose the result that matches the total: hard failure, near miss, mixed success, strong success, exceptional success, or Critical Success.

Quick reference

Official Condition Cards

Player-safePrint-readyTV-safe

Hidden, Restrained, Vulnerable. Module effects stay inside their stat block or scene text and are not global conditions.

Quick reference

Loot Cards

Player-safePrint-ready

Pocket Ward, Stride Salve, Grindstone Vial, Lark-Moth Lantern, Bramble-Cutter's Hook, Compliance Stamp, Firstmoss Poultice, Mixed Chits, Whetcord, Tinker's Kit, Soul-Quiet Charm, Strixwolf-Down Cloak.

Quick reference

Delivery Manifest

Player-safePrint-readySpoilers

ASSET, SEALED - do not open. Chain-of-custody initials do not match the cart route times.

Quick reference

Goldwater Slip

Player-safePrint-readySpoilers

Payment overdue. Ward continuity riders remain enforceable regardless of route interruption.

Quick reference

Hexmart Pocket Ward Card

Player-safePrint-ready

Budget consumer charm. Cracked. It did not save Tamsin, but it explains what kind of safety ordinary people can afford.

Quick reference

Bramble Route Sketch

Player-safePrint-readySpoilers

A hand-drawn map of official routes that skip displaced settlements. Useful evidence, not proof of innocence.

Daggerheart Table Support

Use this when a player asks what to roll.

Roll in 10 Seconds

roll check skill check action rolls 2d12 hope die fear die DC difficulty class hinge crit critical doubles
  • Pick the trait that matches the approach.
  • Set the Difficulty before the roll matters.
  • State the stakes.
  • Roll Hope d12 + Fear d12.
  • Add trait, Experience, and bonuses.
  • Compare total to Difficulty.
Action RollOfficialDuality DiceOfficialDifficultyOfficialCritical SuccessOfficial

Read total first, then Hope/Fear spin.

Action Roll Results

roll check skill check action rolls with Hope hope spend spend Hope with Fear GM Fear fear spend crit critical doubles
  • Critical Success: best outcome, gain Hope, clear 1 Stress.
  • Success with Hope: they get it and gain Hope.
  • Success with Fear: they get it, but cost or pressure enters.
  • Failure with Hope: they miss, but gain Hope and a useful thread.
  • Failure with Fear: they miss and the GM makes a stronger move.

Fast handles for rules that come up mid-session but do not deserve a lecture.

GM Screen Edge Cases

group action group action roll group roll team action fate roll chance roll luck roll temporary temporary tag temporary condition temporary effect falling fall damage collision crash dangerous speed spellcast spellcast roll spell roll cast a spell unarmed punch kick improvised punch
  • Group Action: choose a leader; helpers roll reactions; successes and failures shift the leader's roll.
  • Fate Roll: define the stakes, then roll one Duality Die when the outcome is pure chance.
  • Temporary effects: clear through the listed move, natural end, or GM/Fear procedure if a spell says so.
  • Falling or collision: use the SRD damage guide and fit the danger to the fiction.
  • Spellcast Roll: only when a feature calls for the character's Spellcast trait.
  • Unarmed attack: Strength or Finesse, then Proficiency d4 damage on a hit.

#rules-canon

Action Roll Flow

['roll', 'check', 'skill check', 'action rolls'] ['saving throw', 'save', 'reaction'] ['group action', 'group action roll', 'group roll', 'team action']

Ask what the PC does, choose the trait that matches the fictional approach, set or reveal the Difficulty, then roll.

Roll Duality Dice, add the trait and any applicable Experience or bonus, compare the total to the Difficulty, then read Hope/Fear spin.

Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and the consequence matters. If there is no meaningful pressure, give the result without a roll.

#rules-canon

Duality Dice

['2d12', 'hope die', 'fear die']

Official default: roll two d12s, one Hope die and one Fear die.

Total the dice, add the relevant trait and bonuses, then compare to Difficulty.

The higher die determines whether the roll is with Hope or with Fear. Matching dice are a Critical Success.

Reaction rolls use the Duality Dice structure, but they do not generate Hope or Fear.

#rules-canon

Hope/Fear Outcomes

TotalSpinResult
>= DifficultyHopeSuccess with Hope: get what you want and gain Hope.
>= DifficultyFearSuccess with Fear: get what you want, but there is a cost or consequence; GM gains Fear.
< DifficultyHopeFailure with Hope: things do not go as planned, but gain Hope.
< DifficultyFearFailure with Fear: things go badly; major consequence or complication; GM gains Fear.

#rules-canon

Critical Success

['crit', 'critical', 'doubles']

When the Hope die and Fear die match, the roll is a Critical Success.

A Critical Success counts as a roll with Hope even if the total would otherwise miss the Difficulty.

On a Critical Success, the PC gains Hope and clears 1 Stress. On an attack roll, follow the official critical damage rules.

#gm-aid not official

D&D-to-Daggerheart Translation

D&D Conversion

Daggerheart uses traits, not D&D skills. Pick the trait that matches the player's fictional approach.

Use the D&D conversion page as a GM aid for players arriving from 5e; it is not official Daggerheart rules text.

#rules-canon

Advantage / Disadvantage

['advantage', 'disadvantage']

Advantage adds a d6 advantage die to the roll total.

Disadvantage subtracts a d6 disadvantage die from the roll total.

Advantage and disadvantage cancel each other out before rolling. If multiple advantage dice remain, use the highest one.

The GM may grant advantage or disadvantage when the fiction supports it.

#rules-canon

Experiences, Help, Tag Team

Experiences are short backstory/expertise phrases. Spend 1 Hope before a roll to add a relevant Experience modifier.

Help an Ally: spend 1 Hope, describe feasible help, roll a d6 advantage die, and add it to the acting PC's roll using the normal advantage rules.

Tag Team Roll: once per session, spend 3 Hope to combine two PCs' efforts. Both roll, choose one result for both, and resolve as a single action roll.

#rules-canon

Hope Uses / Fear Uses

['with Hope', 'hope spend', 'spend Hope'] ['Sablewood Hope Moments', 'Sablewood Fear Moments', 'hope moments', 'fear moments']

Hope can be spent to Help an Ally, use Experiences, initiate a Tag Team Roll, or activate Hope Features.

On a roll with Fear, the GM gains Fear and makes a move reflecting the complication.

Fear can be spent to spotlight adversaries, use Fear Features, make stronger GM moves, apply adversary Experiences, and advance pressure when the rules or stat block call for it.

#rules-canon

GM Moves / Adversary Spotlight

['GM Move', 'make a move'] ['rules drawer', 'quick reference'] GM MovesAdversary Spotlight

The spotlight moves through the fiction rather than a fixed initiative order.

The GM commonly makes moves when a PC rolls with Fear or fails an action roll.

Use softer moves to telegraph, reveal, or reposition. Use harder moves when the fiction and result call for direct consequence.

Spend Fear or use features when the adversary/environment rules call for it.

#rules-canon

Adversary Attack Rolls

['enemy attack', 'attack roll', 'adversary attack'] Adversary Attack Rolls

Adversaries roll a d20 plus their attack modifier against the target PC's Evasion.

PCs do not roll defense by default. Use reaction rolls only when a rule, feature, or GM call gives one.

PC action rolls against adversaries use the adversary's Difficulty from the stat block.

#rules-canon

Damage / Armor / Stress

['damage', 'threshold', 'thresholds'] ['falling', 'fall damage', 'collision', 'crash', 'dangerous speed'] ['damage die', 'damage dice', 'weapon damage'] Damage / Armor

Compare incoming damage to the character's damage thresholds to determine how many HP are marked.

Mark an Armor Slot to reduce the severity of incoming damage by one threshold.

When a character marks their last Stress, they become Vulnerable until they clear at least 1 Stress.

If a character must mark Stress while all Stress slots are marked, follow the official overflow consequence from the character rules.

#rules-canon

Short Rest

['rest', 'Prepare', 'Tend to Wounds', 'Clear Stress', 'Repair Armor']

A short rest is about an hour to catch breath and recover.

Each PC may swap domain cards between loadout and vault, then choose two moves, including choosing the same move twice.

Short rest moves: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, or Prepare.

Prepare gains Hope; preparing with one or more party members gives each of those PCs 2 Hope.

#rules-canon + module tracker

Countdown

['clock', 'timer', 'countdown']

Countdowns are visible pressure clocks. Tell players what changes when a countdown ticks.

On progress countdowns, successful action rolls can tick the party closer to the goal.

On consequence countdowns, failures or success with Fear can tick the opposing pressure closer.

Open Vale uses a module ritual countdown as a tracker; do not treat it as a new condition.

#rules-canon

Ranges

['range', 'movement', 'distance']

Use Daggerheart range bands at the table: Melee, Very Close, Close, Far, Very Far, and Out of Range.

When exact distance is not important, keep ranges conversational and tied to reachable action.

#rules-canon

Official Conditions

Official Conditions

Daggerheart has three primary global conditions: Hidden, Restrained, and Vulnerable.

Some features create unique effects, but those are feature-specific text, not module-wide conditions.

Unless a rule says otherwise, the same condition cannot stack on one target.

Temporary conditions can be cleared with a fitting action roll, a GM-approved fictional method, or by an adversary spending its spotlight to clear the condition.

Unconscious appears only as Death Move/status context in this Atlas, not as a global condition card.
